name: International OCD Foundation (IOCDF)
description: Support groups, resources, and community for people with OCD and related disorders. Find local chapters worldwide.

sections.title: About the International OCD Foundation
sections.text: The International OCD Foundation (IOCDF) is a donor-supported nonprofit organization serving the global OCD community. Founded in 1986 by a small group of individuals with OCD, the IOCDF has grown into the leading resource for people affected by OCD and related disorders including body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), hoarding disorder, trichotillomania (hair pulling), and skin picking disorder. The organization's mission is to help everyone affected by OCD and related disorders live full and productive lives.

sections.title: Educational Resources
sections.text: IOCDF provides comprehensive educational materials about OCD and related disorders, including detailed information about symptoms, causes, and evidence-based treatments. Resources cover the distinction between OCD and normal worrying, common OCD subtypes (contamination, harm, religious/scrupulosity, relationship), and guidance for family members. The foundation publishes articles, videos, and guides written and reviewed by leading OCD experts. Their website features first-person stories from people living with OCD who have found effective treatment.

sections.title: Finding OCD Treatment
sections.text: IOCDF maintains a searchable Resource Directory of mental health professionals who specialize in treating OCD using Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), the gold-standard treatment for OCD. You can search for therapists by location, specialty, and treatment approach. The foundation provides guidance on what to look for in an OCD specialist, questions to ask potential providers, and information about intensive treatment programs for severe OCD. They also offer resources about medication options that may complement therapy.

sections.title: Support Groups and Community
sections.text: IOCDF has a network of local affiliates and support groups across the United States and internationally. Support groups provide a space for people with OCD and their family members to share experiences, coping strategies, and encouragement. The foundation hosts the Annual OCD Conference, the largest gathering of OCD community members, researchers, and clinicians in the world. Online communities and forums connect people with OCD year-round, helping reduce the isolation that often accompanies the disorder.

sections.title: Specialized Programs and Initiatives
sections.text: IOCDF runs specialized programs including the Pediatric OCD Program for children, teens, and families; the OCD in the Workplace initiative addressing accommodation and disclosure issues; and the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiative to ensure culturally responsive OCD care. The foundation funds research grants to advance understanding and treatment of OCD. Advocacy efforts focus on improving insurance coverage for OCD treatment and increasing access to specialized care across underserved communities.
